job.style: a passage that starts from a common wrong idea and corrects it

response.passage: Many people believe that if a caller knows their name or claims to be from a bank, they are trustworthy and must follow instructions immediately to avoid account closure. This is a dangerous myth. Banks will never ask you to share your OTP, PIN, or CVV over a phone call, even if they claim it is for a KYC update. If you receive a message asking you to click a link to update your KYC, do not click it, as legitimate banks do not operate this way. Furthermore, some scammers promise high monthly returns on investments and ask you to keep the deal secret from your family. They might even show you a fancy office or a certificate to look official. Remember, a high-return scheme that requires secrecy is almost always a fraud. If you ever lose money, do not wait or feel ashamed; report the incident immediately to the official cybercrime portal or your bank. Never trust a phone number provided by a stranger; always use the official contact details found on the back of your debit card or the bank's verified website. By staying alert and never sharing your secret banking codes, you can keep your money safe from those who try to trick you.
response.summary: Scammers often use fake urgency and official-looking documents to steal money. You should never share your secret banking codes like OTPs or PINs with anyone. Always verify information through official bank channels rather than trusting strangers.
